```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation for single-targeting projects (which both LibA and LibB are). **Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, where `$(TargetFramework)` is reliably populated:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults in `.targets` override project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–11

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` files are imported **after** the project file. MSBuild uses last-write-wins for properties, so these values unconditionally override anything set in individual `.csproj` files. This directly causes the next finding — LibB's `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` is silently overridden back to `true`.

The metadata properties (`Company`, `Authors`, `Copyright`) also cannot be overridden per-project, though that may be intentional.

**Fix:** Move **defaultable** properties to `Directory.Build.props` with conditional guards:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 3. `LibB/LibB.csproj` — `TreatWarningsAsErrors` override is silently ignored
**File:** `LibB/LibB.csproj`, line 13

```xml

```

**Fix:** Fix is in Finding #2 above — once defaults move to `.props` with conditions, this project-level override will work correctly.

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** Two issues here:
1. **Overwrites instead of appending:** This kills `DEBUG` and `TRACE` constants that the SDK defines by default. Any `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` blocks in code will stop working.
2. **Unquoted condition:** `$(Configuration) == Debug` should be `'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'`. If `Configuration` is empty, this evaluates to ` == Debug` which MSBuild may misparse.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
  <DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 5. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Publish-on-build target forks a racing second build instance
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This re-invokes the same project via `<MSBuild>` with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). MSBuild treats this as a **distinct project instance** (same path but different global properties), which triggers a full re-evaluation and rebuild. Both instances write to the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, creating a **file race condition** that causes intermittent build failures.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish within the same project instance, or use a dedicated publish step in CI rather than coupling it to Build.

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Wrong F# source file order
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** In F#, **file order in the `.fsproj` is the compilation order**, and files can only reference types/modules from files listed **above** them. `Services.fs` has `open BrokenOrder.Domain`, but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* `Services.fs`. This will produce a **compile error** (FS0039: namespace/module not found).

Compare with `OrderService/OrderService.fsproj` which has the correct order: `Domain.fs` → `Services.fs` → `Program.fs`.

**Fix:**
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```

### 7. `LibA/LibA.csproj` & `LibB/LibB.csproj` — Hardcoded absolute `OutputPath`
**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 7, `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** These are Windows-specific absolute paths. The build will fail or produce unexpected results on Linux/macOS (CI agents, containers, devs on Mac). This also means the path doesn't vary by `Configuration`, so Debug and Release builds overwrite each other.

**Fix:** Use a relative or repo-rooted path with configuration:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)..\artifacts\bin\$(MSBuildProjectName)\$(Configuration)\</OutputPath>
```
Or better yet, use the modern [artifacts output layout](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/sdk/artifacts-output) by adding `<UseArtifactsOutput>true</UseArtifactsOutput>` in `Directory.Build.props`.

### 8. `Directory.Build.props` — Analyzer package missing `PrivateAssets`
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, line 17

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, this analyzer package **leaks to downstream consumers**. Any project that references LibA/LibB via NuGet would transitively pull in StyleCop.Analyzers, which is almost never the desired behavior.

  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

### 9. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Legacy direct assembly reference instead of PackageReference
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–29

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">

**Problem:** This is a legacy `packages.config`-style direct assembly reference pointing into a `packages/` folder. In an SDK-style project, this should be a `PackageReference`. ```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

### 10. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Redundant explicit `Compile Include` causes duplicate (CS2002)
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 21–23

```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```

**Problem:** The SDK automatically includes all `*.cs` files via implicit globbing. The explicit `<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />` creates a **duplicate entry**, which may produce CS2002 ("Source file specified multiple times") warnings. The `Update` in the same `ItemGroup` as the `Include` can also have subtle evaluation-order issues.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```
